sources.topic: Pre-launch hour: openers to hold, items to slam or avoid, fast 9 and level 8 flex boards, emblems, wisp strategy

earlyGame: Early-game goal is gold plus HP: strong openers that win-streak stage 2 and most of stage 3 let you reach 80-90 HP at 4-1 and fast 9 (Iverson).
Best openers: 2 Ravagers plus 2 frontliners (Camille is the premier one; Akali and Diana are Ravagers, Akali is AP-or-AD adaptable) (Iverson).
Pick Brawler or Juggernaut as the opener frontline; Defender is the weakest frontline package and gets the lowest hold priority (Iverson).
Blossom opener: hold every Blossom unit, field 3 Blossom by 1-4 to get the special upgraded Blossom wisp at 2-1, then add a Juggernaut and a Spellweaver (Karma, Yorick(?)) (Iverson).
Master Yi from an orb plus any frontline can take over stage 2 by himself; he holds almost any item and is also Blossom (Iverson).
Teemo plus 2 Brawler (or 2 Blackthorn without sacrificing) is a good opener because he farms about half a gold per fight and Brawlers are very tanky (Iverson).
Strong holds are the 3-costs: Cassiopeia, Diana, Fiddlesticks (healing tank), Rengar (farms gold), Vi, Krug (splits into two), Master Yi; weaker holds are Azir and Tristana (Iverson).
Whether to hold mid 1-costs like Pebbles or Cinderling depends on the components you have: they are worthless without a slam (Cinderling wants Shojin) (Iverson).
Karma scales better off damage items than mana items because she spends most of her time casting; Karma 2 beats Yunara 1, Yunara 2 beats Karma 2 (Iverson).

Slam priority for stage 2: Warmog's and Stone Plate are the best tank slams, Shojin is the most flexible, Blue Buff is about as good as Shojin, Infinity Edge is a safe open slam, Rageblade is very strong but forces Draven or Nidalee (Iverson).
Slam Crown Guard when you are AD (it eats a spare rod) and Giant Slayer when you are AP (it eats a spare sword and bow); the reverse is a poor slam (Iverson).
Void Staff and Last Whisper beat Shroud and Spark for shred; you need some shred/sunder from Kog'Maw, Kayle or an item (Iverson).

Avoid slamming Bloodthirster, Hodge(?), Striker's Flail without another crit item, Nashor's Tooth below 100% crit, Adaptive Helm, Archangel's on carries that prefer Death Cap, and (early) Gunblade; Titan's and Sterak's are fine on fighters (Iverson).
Do not slam Bramble Vest or Dragon's Claw until you know the lobby: Bramble into an AD lobby, Dragon's Claw into an AP lobby, otherwise take Stone Plate or Warmog's (Iverson).
Because Inferno gives burn and wound, Sunfire, Morellonomicon and Red Buff are lower-priority slams this set (Iverson, BM, Tactician's Institute).
Use consumables and stat shards on early item holders instead of hoarding them for the final carry, since early and mid game often matter more than a greedy endgame (BM).
Wisps (this set's mechanic) show up every other shop in the rightmost slot, only one can be bought per round, and they vanish when combat starts (all three).
Early game, buy econ wisps and zero-cost wisps; skip 2-gold combat wisps unless one saves a crucial streak, because losing gold breaks interest breakpoints (Iverson).
Before clicking any gold wisp, check which 10-gold interest breakpoint it makes you miss; Free Roller (pay 2 for 2 rolls) is often a net loss near 10 or 20 gold (Iverson).
To see a wisp every round instead of every other round, roll once more each turn; free-roll sources like Trade Sector make this cheaper (BM, Tactician's Institute).
If you are rolling down anyway, buy the first acceptable wisp you see so you stop wasting a shop slot, then keep rolling for units (BM, Tactician's Institute).
Zero-gold-wisp trick: spend so you have exactly 2 gold, roll, and the game will offer a wisp you can afford; after the nerf, leaving 1 gold may now be better (Iverson).
Read each wisp fully: some need you to win the round, some upgrade shop units to full price (a 2-star 1-cost then costs 3), and Animate Shop only helps if you have bench space (BM).
In 1-cost reroll, never click an XP wisp in stage 2; it pushes you to level 5 at 3-1 and wrecks the plan (BM).
Streaking: win streak and lose streak both generate the most gold; a mixed streak is the worst, so pick a lane by 2-3 or 2-5 and commit (BM).
On launch-week lobbies, win-streaking with a strong opener into fast 9 is the simplest high-win-rate plan; lose streak only if you have a known powerful line (Iverson).
augmentPrinciples: Stage 2 (2-1) augment: if you plan to lose-streak, you must take an econ augment (or one that scales with time/low HP); an item or combat augment on a lose streak wastes the game (BM).
Stage 2 augment on a strong opener or win streak: take emblem/trait augments or combat power so you keep winning; econ is optional (BM, Iverson).
Econ augments are indirectly stronger this set because wisps cost gold, so a build with no econ augment ends up broke (BM).
Any augment that gives free rerolls is better this set, since it lets you see a wisp every round (BM, Tactician's Institute).
Emblem augments are top priority: instantly click Spreading Roots, Branching Out and Trait Ladder; happily click The Trait Tree and Flexible; Tactician's Kitchen is A-tier (Iverson).
Frontline Foundation and Backline Blueprint (transcript says 'front/backline blueprint') are good when you need direction; the Defender version is awkward (Iverson).
Portable Forge is a strong stage 2 pick: most artifacts lead into Master Yi (Hydra, Witsend, RFC, Fishbones, Hellfire Hatchet, Midens, Flicker Blades) (Iverson).
Destiny augments (random augment) are above the power budget, so take them when you are open to anything and do not yet know your plan (BM).
Random-output augments are balanced slightly above average, so they are usually fine to click (BM).
Trait-specific gold augments such as Nature's Shelter and Omega Riftbeast give you units, an upgrade and direction when you were directionless, as long as you roll that unit pair (BM).

Only take an augment that needs a payoff you can reach: Nesting Dolls needs 3-star units, Seraphim's Staff needs 2-3 Archangels by stage 3, Birthday Present/Reunion needs you to reach level 9 for a 2-star 5-cost (BM).
Take greedy/gold-scaling augments (Capital Gains) when your opener is weak and you will lose-streak or when you have a gold opener; they convert to a roll-down or 4-1 power spike (BM).
Take Hard Bargain only with a good-or-better opener and a plan to win or mix streak; if you lose-streak with it your game is likely over (BM).
Wisp Rebate and Residual Magic are for players who will buy a wisp every turn, which usually means a reroll comp; fast 8/9 players should not take Residual Magic (BM).
Pick augments that fit your actual HP and board: on high HP take scaling or econ, on low HP take immediate combat power (BM, Iverson).
Before clicking, make sure you know what an unfamiliar augment does; a wrong click costs the whole game, so prefer ones whose payoff you have already planned (BM).

fast8: Win-streak timing: level 4 at 2-1, 5 at 2-5, 6 at 3-1, 7 at 3-5, 8 at 4-2, 9 at 5-2 (BM).
Level 8 is the standard plan about 80% of the time; its strongest tempo is 4-2 (BM).
Win-streak level 8: do the whole roll-down at 4-2; with a leveling augment you can roll to zero and still reach 9 in stage 5 (BM).
Without an econ augment, roll at 4-2 until you have a 2-star 4-cost carry and tank; a 1-star secondary carry is fine, wait and add it at level 9 (BM).
Mix streak: level 4 at 2-1 or 2-3, 5 at 2-5 or 3-1, 6 at 3-2, 7 at 3-5 or 4-1, 8 at 4-2 or 4-5, 9 at 5-2 or 5-5 (BM).
Contested lobby: level 8 at 4-2; uncontested: 4-5 is okay; on a mixed streak just play for top 4 (BM).
Lose-streak fast 8: level 4 at 2-3, 5 at 2-7, 6 at 3-2, 7 at 3-5 only if you have 40+ gold, 8 at 4-1 and roll then (BM).
Lose-streak 8 lets you hit 4-costs before everyone else and you must win every stage 4 round (BM).
Iverson's low-roll route: level 8 at 4-1 to try to steal a win against level-7 players, then sack 4-2 until the stage 5 neutral round.
fast9: Fast 9 needs a win streak (or big econ) and a stable opener; the typical plan is to reach 4-1 around 80-90 HP, level 8 at 4-1 or 4-2, then sack stage 4 (Iverson, BM).
Roll for 10-20 gold at 4-2 only to upgrade key pairs (3-/4-cost); otherwise do not roll, and aim to arrive at 5-2 with about 50 gold (BM).
If you enter stage 4 with a 2-star 3-cost carry and tank you can lose rounds for 10-15 HP each and still reach 5-2 safely; if you have only 1-star 4-costs or 2-cost 2-stars, roll a bit first (BM).
At 5-2 with level 9: pick the team in the planner, roll down, then slam items on whoever gets 2-star (BM).
Level 9 costs about 68 gold from level 8; do not go 9 if your 4-costs are not 2-star, since a 50-gold roll-down at 8 usually makes more units 2-star than one extra 1-star slot (BM).
Fast 9 usually needs at least one econ augment to pass level 9 (Iverson); lose-streaking into fast 9 is risky and only works with stacked econ augments, reaching 9 at 4-3 to 4-5 (BM).
Draven Fast 9: needs Rageblade, an AD item (IE, Death Blade or Kraken) and Last Whisper; do the pivot by 4-5 to 5-1 for scaling (Iverson).
Fast 9 has tanks, supports and carries, so any items you have will fit someone in this set (BM).
reroll1: 1-cost reroll: roll at level 4 (sometimes level 5); stage 2 is max econ while buying every key 1-cost unit (BM).
At 3-1 stay at level 4 and roll down to 32 gold; if you are one unit from the 3-star carry roll further, if you are far, econ back to 50 and slow roll (BM).
Second roll-down at 3-5 only if you are 1-2 units off; at 4-1 roll to zero to finish the 3-star tank and 3-star damage dealer, then power level (BM).
1-cost reroll spikes at 3-1, 3-5 and early 4-1; win the first 1-2 rounds of stage 4, then it falls off (BM).
Never take an XP wisp or XP augment in stage 2 during 1-cost reroll (BM).
Two main 3-stars (front and back) cost about 18 gold of units, so this line is cheap and forgiving for beginners (BM).
reroll2: 2-cost reroll is best from a lose streak: level 4 at 2-3, 5 at 2-7, 6 at 3-2, then 7/8/9 whenever convenient (BM).
Make maximum interest in stage 2, hold the units you want, then do a big roll-down at 3-2 and win every stage 3 round from 3-2 on (BM).
2-star 2-cost carry with 2+ items wins most games in stage 3; then slow roll (econ to 50, roll down to 50 each turn) and all-in to 0 when ready (BM).
Win-streak version: level 4 at 2-1, level 5 at 2-5, then the same plan (BM).
Spikes at 3-2, 4-1 and 4-5; with a reroll augment like Prismatic Ticket, 3-stars come around 4-1 (BM).
reroll3: 3-cost reroll is for lose streaks (and win streaks if you have a star 3-cost carry): level 4 at 2-3, 5 at 2-7, 6 at 3-2, 7 at 3-5 with 40+ gold (BM).
Only play it if you found the 3-cost from a starting orb or you have a great augment/artifact; do the big roll-down at 3-5 (BM).
Win-streak variant: level 4 at 2-1, 5 at 2-5, 6 at 3-2, 7 at 3-5; level 5 at 2-5 only if you keep more than 20 gold or are sure to win-streak (BM).
Spikes at 3-5 (2-star 3-costs), 4-1 and 5-1 (3-stars); rarely go to level 8 before stage 5 because it is very expensive (two 3-star 3-costs cost 54 gold in units alone) (BM).
general: Level up when you can keep at least 30 gold after leveling to 7, 8 or 9; below that you need a clear reason (BM).
Four questions before leveling: how much gold remains, do I need to level and roll the same turn, what shop odds do I want, and does leveling protect my streak (BM).
Optimal roll levels: 1-cost level 4 (or 5), 2-cost level 6, 3-cost level 7, 4-cost level 8, 5-cost level 9; hybrid 1+2 cost rolls at level 5 (BM).

Hybrid 1+2 (Kayle/Solar): stay level 5, arrive at level 5 around 2-7 to 3-2 (not 2-5), slow roll at 50 gold, and 3-star everything by mid stage 4; go to level 6 once you have 6-8 copies of each 1-cost (BM).
Hybrid with a strong opener (win 3 of 5 stage 2 fights): level 4 at 2-1 is acceptable (BM).
Save gold when you have not reached your roll level, when you are healthy (80 HP at stage 5 can greed to 9), or when your board is already strong with empty bench (BM).
Roll when you need immediate strength, need to preserve HP, have pairs/outs at your best level; with 2-3 pairs count 1-star units you still need as outs too (BM).
Level to activate a key trait (especially 3-trait units like Rakan, Yorick(?)) if that is more impactful than anything else (BM).
Scout your matchup pool before leveling: do not break the 30-gold rule if leveling will not change the outcome against the players you actually face (BM).
Late game: stay above about 10 gold in stage 5+ if possible so you can afford a busted combat wisp; roll to zero is riskier in this set (BM).
Once your board is hit and HP is low (e.g. 20 HP at 4-5) roll for a combat wisp every turn; with 70 HP just be greedy toward level 9 (Iverson).
During a big roll-down it is usually better to buy a 2-gold combat wisp to free the shop slot than to roll hoping for an econ wisp (Iverson).
Aim for a 2-star board by 4-2 to 5-1; fast 8/9 players spike at 4-2 (or 5-2 for level 9) (BM).

comps.advice: Rageblade is mandatory; add an AD item and Last Whisper; frontline is flexible (Maokai 2-star is the best frontliner), Ezreal is a strong second carry; pivot by 4-5 to 5-1 for scaling; his best quest is 8,000 damage for 7 gold (Iverson).
Elder Dragon (cleaves adjacent enemies) is expected to be strong; with 10 Rift Beasts Elder Dragon also gives +2 team size, but 10 Rift Beasts is not an auto-win (Iverson, Tactician's Institute).
Level 8 flexible board (Aphelios, Diana, Brambleback, Rapid Fire); frontline can be Sett+Krug or Hecarim+Sentinel; low-roll top-4 board that rarely wins; do not 2-star Zyra here (Iverson).
Level 8 AP flex around 2 Flora Fatalis (Fiddlesticks, Soraka), Azir and a Blackthorn-fed Malphite; very flexible when low-rolling (Iverson).

Solar/Kayle is a hybrid 1+2 cost reroll that caps around top 4 and needs 5 three-star units, so prefer a good opener or a reroll augment like Prismatic Ticket; Kayle provides shred (BM, Tactician's Institute, Iverson).
Fae-emblem enabled reroll; Rengar and Kha'Zix rivals scale but need an early orb and an item slam (Iverson, Tactician's Institute).
Get Kha'Zix early from an orb and slam an item immediately; he evolves with takedowns (Tactician's Institute, Iverson).
Blossom emblem is premium: force 7 Blossom at level 8 for 4 gold a turn, use that to reach 9, then pivot to 5 Blossom plus legendaries (Iverson, Tactician's Institute).
Takes over stage 2, needs artifacts or a Brawler emblem to reroll; keep his frontline alive so he is not killed early (Iverson).
Ahri is the highest-cap level 9 AP carry; Morgana is a great Morellonomicon+Void Staff holder (Iverson).

commonMistakes: Going to level 9 too early (before your 4-costs are 2-star) instead of rolling at 8 (BM).
Forcing a level-up on a win streak without checking whether it changes the outcome against the matchups you face (BM).
Rolling with an empty bench or nothing to look for (BM).
Clicking an augment you do not understand, or an augment whose payoff you cannot reach (BM).
Taking an econ-less augment while planning to lose-streak (BM).
Autoclicking an XP wisp while in 1-cost reroll (BM).
Buying gold wisps without checking interest breakpoints (Iverson).
Spending gold on a 2-gold combat wisp in the early or mid game (Iverson).
Slamming Bramble or Dragon's Claw before scouting AD/AP lobby, or Striker's/Nashor's without crit (Iverson).
Building mana items on specialist (no-mana) units like Caitlyn, Kayle, Nar (BM).
Rolling to zero gold in stage 5+ and being unable to afford a combat wisp (BM).
Forgetting Young and Wild and Free or other carousel-dependent augments (BM).
conflicts: Rageblade: BM says few good 4-cost users and prefers upfront AS like Red Buff on Aphelios; Iverson is happy to slam it early but calls it forcing Draven/Nidalee, and says Aphelios can use it though not best-in-slot.
Inferno 3 shop upgrade: BM likes it to cheese a 5-cost at level 8, Tactician's Institute says it is not worth the extra unit and 2 Inferno is the sweet spot.
Elderwood: Tactician's Institute says only play the vertical with an emblem, while Iverson likes Elderwood Draven fast 9 and Lux Elderwood for breakpoints.
Combat wisps: Iverson says skip 2-gold combat wisps early and mid game, BM says buy the first acceptable wisp during roll-downs to avoid wasting shop slots.
Win vs lose streak: Iverson prefers win streaking into fast 9 on day one; BM treats both as equal and gives lose-streak a faster level 8 at 4-1.
Late-game gold: BM wants about 10 gold held in stage 5+ for combat wisps; Iverson says to roll for combat wisps every turn when low HP and be greedy when high HP.
Standard-play level 5 timing: BM's win-streak table uses 2-5, but for hybrid 1+2 reroll he says avoid 2-5 and wait until 2-7 to 3-2.
